plan: Something is assembled in the dark, piece by piece, and once it is whole it does not stop. Steel until the turn at 48s, blood after it, white twice.

states.why: INTRO — the pars are OFF. Four lamps cannot make a statement; the head can. This is the faintest legal glow so the room is not a void, and everything you actually see in the first half minute is the beam and the blackouts between the statements.

INSTRUMENTAL — still the head's half. The track here is four statements separated by holes, the last of them nearly six seconds long. A wash across this would fill in the silences that are the whole point of the passage.

THE TURN. Steel becomes blood here and never goes back. The colour is the event — the level barely moves across the boundary, so what you register is that the room has changed its mind, not that it got brighter.
Second chorus. White starts bleeding into the red — the room is running out of places to go, which is what makes the peak inside this section land.
The song's loudest stretch. It sits high BETWEEN hits, not only on them, so the section reads as the biggest thing in the show even in the gaps.
After the break. Embers rather than blood: the act is done. It lands under the opening, or it is not an ending.

MONEY MOMENT 1 — out of the longest silence in the track (5.9 seconds), landing exactly on a downbeat. This is the reveal the whole opening has been saving for, and no earlier show used it.

MONEY MOMENT 2 — THE TURN at 48.44s. Red, not white: the point is the change of colour, not a flash. The band stops at 47.65 and returns here, so this is the first frame of the second half of the song.
two beats of nothing before the peak
MONEY MOMENT 3 — THE PEAK at 92.50s. The score calls this the loudest stretch of the song and the recording's loudest half-second is the same moment. The only white in the second half.
the head is IN the peak. It was dark there — the pars at full and the only fixture that can point at anything sitting out the biggest moment in the show.
MONEY MOMENT 4 — out of the late break. 2.5 seconds of nothing, back on the downbeat at 111.99s.
17.8s — tempo moves 89 to 119 bpm
83.3s — a build. The score measures its run-up at 4s, so the ramp is exactly that long.
101.3s — a build. The score measures its run-up at 4s, so the ramp is exactly that long.
115.3s — lead-vocal, tambourine and vocal drop out. A controlled pull-back.
120.3s — the music goes up an octave. A rise, so it blooms and falls.
126.7s — the beat drops away
six beats of hardware strobe into the peak — the only strobe in the show, spent on the only place that has earned it
